Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the call earlier — we need to align on the pen test scope before we engage our security team. Can you confirm whether the penetration test report Redwood provides / will provide covers the following for customers like us:

- Hosted API (Redwood-hosted, multi-tenant) — is the serving runtime + control plane included?

We also need a copy of the most recent pen test report (redacted as needed) and a short matrix that maps which artifacts and components are included per hosting variant. Our timeline: we'd like to have this documented before 2026-08-20 so we can start our internal procurement/compliance review.

Hi Alice — thanks for the note. Below is the canonical description we use internally and share with assessors. I've attached a one-page matrix and network diagram for quick reference.

Summary (by hosting mode):

1) Hosted (Redwood-hosted API)
   - In-scope: Redwood-managed control plane services (auth, routing, telemetry), and the serving runtime instances that process tenant requests in our hosted clusters.
   - Out-of-scope: customer data stored in customer-managed sinks; third-party cloud provider infrastructure (we provide cloud provider attestations separately).

2) Dedicated (reserved GPU pools)
   - In-scope: The dedicated serving nodes and the Redwood orchestration/control plane components that manage them (authentication, model routing, telemetry). We consider the dedicated GPU pool part of Redwood-managed infra when reserved through Redwood Dedicated.
   - Out-of-scope: Customer network segments beyond the dedicated endpoint, customer-managed KMS keys (unless integrated via Redwood-managed connectors), and customer-side application code.

3) Private / VPC (customer-deployed with Redwood control plane or private installer)
   - If Redwood manages the control plane in the customer's VPC: in-scope items include the Redwood control plane services and the connectors we deploy.
   - If the customer operates a fully self-hosted/private installation (on-prem or air-gapped): Redwood will provide guidance and can ship the artifact pack we use for internal testing, but the operational pen test responsibility lies primarily with the customer.

4) On-prem (customer installs in their own datacenter)
   - In-scope for Redwood: distribution artifacts, deployment manifests, known CVE scans we performed, and any support agent components that Redwood ships.
   - In-scope for customer/vendor: network isolation, physical controls, and any downstream integrations. Redwood does not normally perform full network pen tests on customer on-prem environments.

Common exclusions across modes:
- Any third-party SaaS endpoints that customers integrate with (we can provide a list).
- Customer data stores and KMS keys unless the customer requests Redwood-managed key integration and explicitly includes them.

Artifacts we can provide (attached / available):
- scope_matrix_v2.xlsx (maps components -> in-scope per hosting variant)
- redwood_network_diag.pdf (high-level network flows, egress/ingress ranges)
- redacted_pen_test_report_202605.pdf (vendor report, high/critical findings redacted for customer-specific details)
- previous remediation tracker (we can provide Jira links)

Requested from FinServ for HexProbe to run tests:
- The test window(s) you'd like us to support (preferred weekdays, e.g., 8/23-8/27)
- Any IP allowlist for HexProbe test agents to avoid blocking by our WAF (we will temporarily create test ACLs)
- Contact for temporary test accounts (we can provision scoped API keys and test tenant)

I'll attach the matrix and network diagram now. HexProbe, please confirm you have what you need for triage.

-Karthik
